issue.title: Code injection via unescaped f-string interpolation in dspy_slot.py
issue.description: dspy_slot.py lines 202-203 interpolate config.model and config.training_data_path into generated Python source code via f-strings without escaping. If these values come from untrusted input, they could inject arbitrary Python code into the generated script. slot_name is sanitized via _sanitize_name() but model and training_data_path are not.

evidence.before_after_proof: Before: lines 202-203 use f-string interpolation with raw double-quote wrapping: f'..."{config.model}"...' and f'..."{config.training_data_path}"...'. A malicious model value like '" + __import__("os").system("rm -rf /") + "' would break out of the string literal and execute arbitrary code. After: using !r format spec applies repr() which escapes special characters and wraps in appropriate quotes, preventing injection.
evidence.forbidden: Do not claim network_absorbable. Do not modify contracts outside this repo.

proposed_fix.description: Replace raw f-string interpolation of config.model and config.training_data_path with !r format spec (repr()) to safely escape values before embedding in generated Python source code.
proposed_fix.diff_summary: 2 lines changed in src/chip_labs/dspy_slot.py: replaced "{config.model}" with {config.model!r} and "{config.training_data_path}" with {config.training_data_path!r}
proposed_fix.tests_or_smoke: Existing tests should still pass as repr() of normal strings produces valid Python string literals. The fix only affects code generation safety, not runtime behavior for well-formed inputs.

pr.title: fix(dspy_slot): use repr() for model/training_data_path in code generation

review_claim.duplicate_notes: No existing PR addresses this specific code injection vector in dspy_slot.py. Other fixes in the repo address different issues (KeyError, score-or-chain, etc.).
review_claim.risk_notes: Low risk change. repr() of normal strings produces equivalent output. Only edge case: if someone relied on the exact string format of generated code with unescaped special characters, which would be a bug itself.
